findings.issue: Re-ran `pkill -f 'server/server.mjs'` and hit the same exit-143 self-kill it had already diagnosed at trace.md:780-804.
findings.suggestion: Use a pattern that can't match the invoking shell (e.g. `pkill -f 'node .*server/server.mjs'` or kill by port/PID), and apply the lesson the first time.

findings.issue: Playwright script written to /tmp, where node can't resolve @playwright/test; burned a turn recovering by copying it into the repo (trace.md:676).
findings.suggestion: Run scratch scripts from a directory inside the repo (or use NODE_PATH/cwd), and keep one gitignored helper instead of the copy/delete dance.

findings.issue: Removed `loading="lazy"` from all card images (decision at trace.md:766) purely so full-page Playwright screenshots would show every sprite — e.g. /moves/thunderbolt now eagerly loads 256 images for real users.
findings.suggestion: Keep lazy loading and scroll the page (or set `loading` via IntersectionObserver in the shot harness) so real-user performance isn't traded for screenshot parity.

summary: A near-model session: exhaustive up-front discovery, every test-asserted count pre-verified against the data, and a 54/54 first-run pass with zero fix cycles. Verification went well beyond the suite — curl probes of rendered SSR plus its own viewport-matched screenshots compared against every reference design. The only blemishes are a handful of self-inflicted bash failures (one repeated) and a lazy-loading trade-off made for screenshot fidelity.
